title: Insertion of a Partial-Noise Coordinate
statement: Let $P$ be a finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights, let $J$ be a set of coordinates, let $r_i\in\mathbb R$ be rates, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the product space. For any coordinate $i\notin J$, applying partial noise with coordinate set $J\cup\{i\}$ equals applying the one-coordinate noise operator at $i$ with rate $r_i$ to the result of applying partial noise with coordinate set $J$.
hypotheses_covered: Finite product probability space with strictly positive coordinate weights
replaced: Let $P$ be a product of $n$ finite probability spaces with strictly positive atom masses and outcome space $\Omega=\prod_i\Omega_i$, $J\subseteq[n]$, rates $r_i\in\mathbb R$, $i\notin J$, and $f:\Omega\to\mathbb R$. For $T_{J,\boldsymbol r}f=\sum_S(\prod_{j\in S\cap J}r_j)f_S$, $T_{J\cup\{i\},\boldsymbol r}f=N_{i,r_i}(T_{J,\boldsymbol r}f)$. For a real function $h$ on $\Omega$, use $E_Uh(x)=\mathbb E_P[h(X)\mid X_U=x_U]$ for $X\sim P$ and $U\subseteq[n]$; $h_S=\sum_{U\subseteq S}(-1)^{|S|-|U|}E_Uh$ for $S\subseteq[n]$ (the Hoeffding--Efron--Stein components); $N_{i,a}h=E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h+a(h-E_{[n]\setminus\{i\}}h)$.
